title: First Thing: Desperate rescue attempts continue in Nepal to reach hundreds thought to be trapped
text:
Good morning. Rescue teams are working to reach hundreds of people feared trapped in the tunnels and underground areas of half a dozen hydropower projects in Nepal as more than 900 workers were reported missing after the devastating flash floods.
The death toll from the ⁠unprecedented deluge of ice, rock, mud ​and debris that crashed through valleys of Nepal on Wednesday last week has risen to 903 people, with 16 reported dead on the Tibet side of the border. More than 4,000 are missing in Nepal, with another 500 in Tibet. Hundreds of bodies, many unidentified, have been buried in shallow graves.
How large is the rescue operation? Nepal’s prime minister, Balendra Shah, said almost 21,000 security personnel were involved in the rescue operations, besides civilian workers and volunteers. China’s state-run CCTV reported that Beijing had mobilised more than 2,100 rescue workers. The Red Cross has ‌estimated that more than 90,000 people are likely to have been affected by the disaster, which China and some experts linked to the effects of the climate crisis.
Why has the disaster sparked a racism row in Australia? A slew of racist social media comments have been made towards missing Australians. Most of them were on pilgrimages, including to Mount Kailash in Tibet. Mainstream media outlets including News Corp, Channel 7, Channel 10 and Nine have been hit with highly offensive and discriminatory comments on Facebook articles identifying the missing Australians.
Iran has launched retaliatory strikes on airbases in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates after the US attacked Iranian rocket launchers in the strait of Hormuz, the first such hostilities in a month. The last known ‌US strikes on Iran were in late July and the war has reached a stalemate in recent weeks.
The latest exchange of fire was sparked late on Sunday by a US attack on the island of Larak in the strait. Iran’s ⁠Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) said the US attack killed and wounded several soldiers and citizens and ​would be met with “punishment” from ‌Tehran.
What has Donald Trump claimed US forces are doing? Hours after the attacks, the US president, Donald Trump, claimed in a social media post that Iran’s energy hub of Kharg Island was being “blown to smithereens” but gave no further details. The White House and ⁠the US defense department did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Attacking Kharg, which handled 90% of ⁠Iran’s oil exports before the war, would severely disrupt the Islamic republic’s energy trade and put huge pressure on its economy.
Donald Trump and Canada continued a verbal duel at the weekend over the US government’s administrative renaming of Lake Ontario, with the Ontario premier erecting a giant sign saying “Lake Ontario. Now and Always” – and the American president posting an AI video depicting him tearing down an avatar of that sign, erecting a replacement saying Lake America, and dancing to YMCA.
The Wendat Nation grand chief, Pierre Picard, called Trump’s move an attempt to erase Indigenous history. “I want to tell him that it is unacceptable for us, as a nation, to have a president who can eradicate our history, our culture and our identity,” Picard said.
The White House “border czar”, Tom Homan, denied on Sunday that deporting the British far-right commentator Milo Yiannopoulos just a day after being arrested by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) amounted to preferential treatment.
Homan said it was his understanding Yiannopoulos, 41, had overstayed what he believed to be a visitor visa, had not appeared at an immigration hearing and was issued a final order of removal on 22 July. He added: “He had his due process, ordered removed by a federal judge, and ICE removed him. It’s that simple.”
Donald Trump ⁠said NBC’s Kristen ‌Welker should face “rebuke or punishment” from the FCC after she described the success record of political candidates whom the president had endorsed as “mixed”.
Ghislaine Maxwell has virtually run out of legal routes to overturn her conviction for her involvement in Jeffrey Epstein’s abuse of girls and young women, experts say, bar a presidential pardon.
At least eight people have died off the coast of Turkish-occupied northern Cyprus after a ferry capsized. Nearly 20 people are still missing.
The Trump administration is shuttering ⁠two of the three US Department of Agriculture research projects studying cyclospora after the foodborne parasite has ⁠sickened tens of thousands of Americans during the summer.
Michigan’s Democratic US senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed apologized to the state’s Jewish Democratic Caucus for comments he made after an attack on a synagogue in March, which he tied to Israel’s actions in the Middle East.
Mansfield Oil Company of Gainesville is suing KRSM and its president, Syed Kazmi, for allegedly picking up nearly $4m of fuel and not paying for it. KRSM sold some of the fuel to stations that are part of the Freedom Fuel Network, promoted by the Trump administration when drivers were facing higher oil prices amid the war with Iran.
At the sacred prairie of Pe’ Sla in South Dakota, Indigenous and environmental groups banded together to halt drilling. “We’re just not used to winning,” said Dr Valeriah Big Eagle, who directs the Black Hills work of NDN Collective, an Indigenous-led advocacy nonprofit based in Rapid City. “We’re people used to being screwed over by the government at every level.”
This is an incredibly harrowing read about one woman’s attempts to keep her daughter safe from an online predator with ties to the extortion group known as 764. He has been sentenced to decades in prison. We also have this guide to five warning signs for parents about sadistic online exploitation.
Pluto will always be a planet to me. Tim Dowling explores the debate about its status that continues two decades after it was demoted to being a “dwarf planet”.
The secretive state has begun repairs on ageing facilities after being revealed as the worst country for leaks of the potent greenhouse gas.
